newsitem.title: SPAIN: Latam banks seen well positioned as multinationals grow.
newsitem.headline: Latam banks seen well positioned as multinationals grow.

text.p: Latin America's banking sector is well positioned to meet the requirements of foreign companies moving in, offering greater technological sophistication than their counterparts in Asia, banking experts said on Saturday.

Bank of America group executive vice president Daniel Riley said banks in most Latin American countries had an advantage over those in Asia in terms of technological development and the expertise of their staff.

"The region differs from Asia in that there are strong and technologically advanced local banks in most of the countries which will help accelerate the process (by which multinationals get established)," he said in a paper prepared for a seminar on the edge of the Inter-American Development Bank's 38th annual meeting.

Latin America's historically volatile economic conditions, and its experience of high inflation rates and monetary fluctuations, mean the region has also developed some of the world's best cash and treasury managers, he added.
Projects are also in hand across the region to automate individual country clearing systems.
"Given the above, Latin America is a more condusive platform for multinationals than is currently being encountered in Asia," Riley said.

Diana Farrell, a partner at U.S. consulting firm McKinsey & Co, said the growth prospects for the banking industry in Latin American were excellent, but that its domestic banks would face increasing competition from foreign financial institutions.
This would necessitate improvements in efficiency and foreign partnerships to help the local banks acquire the tools they currently lack.
Riley said Latin America was fast becoming the next area of focus for multinationals seeking to replicate their earlier European successes, and were becoming increasingly demanding of local banks.

"Companies more and more are regarding sophisticated and efficient electronic services as a minimum requirement for a banking relationship," he said. --Caroline Brothers, Barcelona newsroom +34 3 424 2659
